The opening position also turns the boundary from divine acts done to the human into an accusation about what the human has not done, and the pressed sound of the word helps the halt feel audible rather than merely logical.

words.prose: {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) does more than negate. It governs {{ar:يَقْضِ}} ({{tr:yaqḍi}}) as a jussive verb and keeps the failure open as not yet fulfilled, so the charge remains a live deficit rather than a closed past denial. In this frame it is not a temporal when or after opener; the following jussive fixes it as not-yet negation over an obligation still awaiting completion. Its scope reaches the object clause {{ar:مَآ أَمَرَهُۥ}} ({{tr:mā amarahū}}), making the unfinished matter the commanded content itself. Coming immediately after {{ar:كَلَّا}} ({{tr:kallā}}), the particle turns rebuke into a grammatical accusation, while its repeated sound with {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:mā}}) helps bind negation to the unnamed object.

words.prose: {{ar:يَقْضِ}} ({{tr:yaqḍi}}) is the shortened Form I imperfect under {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}), so noncompletion is visible in the verb's form as well as in the particle. The clipped pacing and dense closure sound suit a settlement verb at the point where closure is denied. The root range makes the missing act more than generic doing: the human has not brought the commanded matter to its end, settled it, or discharged it as a due claim. The Form I shape keeps that failure at direct fulfillment, not intensification, enabling, reciprocity, or an abstract requirement by another form. Because the verb takes {{ar:مَآ أَمَرَهُۥ}} ({{tr:mā amarahū}}) as its object, the failure is defined by command-content, and the implicit subject is the same human who had been object of divine acts and will be named again in 80:24. Echoes sharpen the local pressure: term-completion in 28:29, divine decree in 17:23, and the command-decision pairing in 33:36 all contrast with this unresolved human execution.

words.prose: {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:mā}}) is the hinge between the completion verb and the command verb. It fills the object slot of {{ar:يَقْضِ}} ({{tr:yaqḍi}}), then receives its content from {{ar:أَمَرَهُۥ}} ({{tr:amarahū}}), so the failure is not left vague: it is what was commanded. At the same time, the relative head leaves the duty unnamed and broad, letting the whole commanded matter stand in view. The visible lengthening and the local sound echo with {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) keep the open content slot audible without making the word interrogative or a second negator.

words.prose: {{ar:أَمَرَهُۥ}} ({{tr:amarahū}}) closes the ayah on the source of obligation. The form is active perfect: the command has already been issued, while the failure lies in the human not fulfilling it. As Form I direct ordering, it does not present the human as lacking permission, entering consultation, receiving appointed authority, or self-authorizing command. Its suffix keeps the human personally inside the command word as recipient, and the implicit commander remains recoverable without being named. Because the verb completes {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:mā}}), the unfinished object becomes an assigned command-matter rather than a single named task. The final position, the hū cadence that recalls the prior suffix chain in 80:21-22, and the command-completion pairing echoed at 33:36 all make the ayah land on an obligation still unsettled.

topics.reason: QAC identifies {{ar:أَمَرَهُۥ}} ({{tr:amarahū}}) as a perfect active Form I verb with an object suffix, so passive recipient-only framing is not the local parse.

topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the object suffix as the commanded person and warns against adding an explicit subject beyond the locally unresolved 3ms commanding subject.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The commanded process remains uncompleted.** `يَقْضِ` activates completion and expiration (`ق ض ي` B004) and perfected execution (`ق ض ي` B005); `أَمَرَهُ` activates command or directive (`ء م ر` B002). The negation supplies noncompletion; I infer that creation, enabling, death, and possible revival establish obligations rather than constituting their fulfillment. The ayah reads as a rupture between being fully made and fully executing what one was directed to do.
2. **A growth-command links moral completion to cultivated provision.** `ء م ر` B004 includes growth and blessing, and the immediately following food sequence makes that branch visible. Combined with `ق ض ي` B005's perfected making, I infer that the human has not brought the directive to mature yield. This is an exploratory process reading: the packet supplies growth and completion branches, while the moral-botanical transfer is mine.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 80:24-32 surprisingly followed noncompletion with a fully executed provision chain. That contrast strengthened perfected execution (`ق ض ي` B005) and growth/blessing (`ء م ر` B004): the surrounding order reaches yield while the human has not.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Human noncompletion is the broken link in a completed sequence.** `ق ض ي B004` supplies completion and expiration. Creation, proportion, path, death-care, and revival at 80:18-22 are each presented as executed stages, while the fixed negation singles out what the human has not finished. I infer a contrast between completed provision and incomplete response. `لَمَّا يَقْضِ` therefore diagnoses failed execution inside an otherwise orderly causal chain.

2. **Perfected making exposes imperfect performance.** `ق ض ي B005` supplies perfected making and carrying an action through. Creation at 80:18-19 and the food process beginning at 80:24-28 supply two enacted systems; human response alone remains unrealized. The packet supplies the parallel sequences, while I infer that their formal completion is the standard against which conduct is read. The verb’s making branch turns the ayah into a contrast of workmanship and nonperformance.

3. **The command is both binding and growth-bearing.** `ء م ر B002` supplies directive or command, distinct from `ء م ر B001` as a generic affair; the governing verb and object pronoun favor the directive branch. Yet `ء م ر B004`, growth and blessing, is activated by food, water, split earth, grain, grapes, and fodder at 80:24-28. I infer that the directive belongs to the same order that enables flourishing. `أَمَرَهُۥ` can thus remain binding without reading as arbitrary coercion.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 80:24-28 answered human noncompletion with a flawlessly completed provision chain. That later execution activated `ق ض ي B005` and made `ء م ر B004` surprising: the binding directive sits inside an order directed toward growth.
